record.paper_title: Dima Khavinson’s 60th: a summary of open problems in analysis and mathematical physics
record.original_question: Let Γ be a real-analytic nonsingular hypersurface in R^n, and let u_Γ be its modified Schwarz potential, meaning a local solution of Δu_Γ = 1 with u_Γ = 0 and ∇u_Γ = 0 on Γ. If the only singularities of u_Γ in R^n are isolated polar singularities x_0 with local behavior u_Γ(x) = O(|x-x_0|^{-m}) for some m > 0, must Γ necessarily be a sphere?

evidence.quote: (2) If u only has isolated “polar” singularities x0 in R^n, i.e., u ∼ O(1/|x−x0|^m), m > 0, near x0, Γ must be a sphere.

artifact.self_contained_problem:
Let $\Gamma \subset \mathbb{R}^n$ ($n \geq 2$) be a real-analytic, nonsingular hypersurface. The modified Schwarz potential of $\Gamma$ is defined as a function $u_\Gamma$, defined in a neighborhood of $\Gamma$, satisfying
$$\Delta u_\Gamma = 1, \qquad u_\Gamma\big|_{\Gamma} = 0, \qquad \nabla u_\Gamma\big|_{\Gamma} = 0.$$
By the Cauchy–Kovalevskaya theorem, such a $u_\Gamma$ exists and is unique in some neighborhood of $\Gamma$, and it admits a (possibly multi-valued) analytic continuation to $\mathbb{R}^n$ outside its singular set.

Suppose that the only singularities of (the analytic continuation of) $u_\Gamma$ in $\mathbb{R}^n$ are isolated polar singularities, i.e., there exist finitely many points $x_0 \in \mathbb{R}^n$ such that, near each such $x_0$,
$$u_\Gamma(x) = O\!\left(|x - x_0|^{-m}\right)$$
for some $m > 0$, and $u_\Gamma$ extends real-analytically to $\mathbb{R}^n$ minus this finite set of points.

Prove or disprove: under these hypotheses, $\Gamma$ must be a sphere.
artifact.status_search_result: The question is part of a circle of conjectures around the Khavinson–Shapiro program on singularities of the Schwarz potential and characterizations of spheres/ellipsoids. Surveys and recent literature (e.g., Lundberg's work on Laplacian/elliptic growth, the AMS Surveys volume 232 by Ebenfelt–Khavinson–Shapiro, and the Notices article "A Tale of Ellipsoids in Potential Theory") discuss this and related conjectures as outstanding problems. No published proof or counterexample establishing that isolated polar singularities of the modified Schwarz potential force $\Gamma$ to be a sphere has been located, so the problem appears to remain open.

status_evidence.title: Laplacian Growth, Elliptic Growth, and Singularities of the Schwarz Potential
status_evidence.snippet: The principal motivation for studying these singularities is to locate the singularities of the Schwarz potential, with applications to Laplacian growth (Hele-Shaw).
status_evidence.claim: Recent survey-type work discusses singularities of the Schwarz potential without resolving the spherical-characterization question.

status_evidence.title: A Tale of Ellipsoids in Potential Theory — Khavinson and Lundberg
status_evidence.snippet: Discusses characterizations of spheres and ellipsoids via potential-theoretic singularity properties.
status_evidence.claim: Spherical/ellipsoidal characterization questions in potential theory are presented as ongoing research.

status_evidence.title: Linear Holomorphic PDE and Classical Potential Theory (AMS Surveys 232)
status_evidence.snippet: Monograph by Ebenfelt, Khavinson and Shapiro covering the Schwarz potential and related conjectures.
status_evidence.claim: The monograph collects conjectures of this type as still-open problems.
